body.p: Claims 1-27 were previously pending with Claims 1, 12, 23, and 27 being independent. Claims 1, 3, 10, 12, 14, 21, and 23 have been amended herein. Claim 27 has been canceled without prejudice or disclaimer and no new claims have been added. Support for the amendments can be found at the least at [0040] - [0044] and FIG. 2. No new matter is added. Accordingly, Claims 1-26 are pending, with claims 1, 12, and 23 being independent. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of the present application, in light of the above amendments and the present remarks.

An interview was held between Examiner Cuevas and Applicant's representative Nathanial Smith (Reg. No. 78,807) on July 27, 2023. The proposed claim amendments were discussed inview of cited art. Examiner Cuevas agreed that the claim amendments overcome the currently cited art. Examiner Cuevas indicated that further analysis would be required. Applicants appreciate the Examiners' time and consideration during the interview.

Claim 27 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102 as being anticipated by U.S. Patent Publication No. 2006/0247508 to Fennell ("Fennell"). Applicant has canceled claim 27 without prejudice or disclaimer.

Claims 1-5, 7, 12-16, and 23-25 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 allegedly obvious over Fennell in view of over U.S. Patent Publication No. 2020/0245910 to Mallas et al. ("Mallas"). Claims 6 and 17 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 allegedly obvious over Fennell in view of Mallas in view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2002/0042561 to Schulman et al. ("Schulman"). As aprimafacie case of the obviousness of claims 1-26 cannot be established based upon the asserted combination of references, Applicant respectfully traverses these rejections as set forth below.
Applicant submits that the claims, as amended with the proposed amendments, are allowable over the cited art.
1. The cited art fails to teach the use of separate voltage sources for the working electrode,
Claim 1 is amended to recite (in part):
provide a working electrode voltage to the working electrode from a working electrode
selectively provide a first counter electrode voltage and a second counter electrode voltage
provide a guard ring voltage to the guard ring from a guard voltage source;
Independent claims 12 and 23 are similarly amended. Support for the amendments can be found at least at [0040] - [0044] and FIG. 2.

Mallas fails to cure the deficiencies of Fennell. Mallas describes using a singular voltage source connected to an operational amplifier to provide power to both the working electrode and the counter electrode. Mallas at [0220]; FIG. 8A. Mallas describes that "the voltage generation or application device 810 supplies a voltage, e.g., the first voltage or the second voltage, to an input terminal of an operational amplifier 840." Mallas at [0220]. As such, "voltage from the voltage generation or application device 810 to the operational amplifier 840 drives a voltage measured at the counter electrode 365." Mallas at [0220]. Mallas also describes that "[t]he voltage generation or application device 810 may also supply the voltage to a working electrode 375 of the sensor 355." Mallas at [0220]. Further, Mallas is silent with respect to the use of a
guard ring. Accordingly, Mallas cannot be relied upon to teach the limitations of the instant claims, as amended.

Furthermore, Schulman fails to cure the deficiencies of Fennell and Mallas. Schulman is silent with respect to the use of a working electrode, counter electrode, and guard ring. Accordingly, Shulman cannot be relied upon to teach the limitations of the instant claims, as amended.
2. Fenell fails to teach the limitation, "guard ring that at least partially surrounds a contact

Fennell does not disclose the limitation "a guard ring that at least partially surrounds a contact region of the working electrode," in Claims 1, 12, and 23. Fennell discloses the use of a guard electrode for leak detection. Fennell at [0028]. Fennell describes that a voltage circuit is coupled to the guard electrode and that "the guard electrode 211 is also coupled to the leak detection circuit 214 of the transmitter 102." Fennell at [0030]. Fennell describes that the leak detection circuit includes a resistor and operatively a capacitor. Fennell at [0035]. Fennell also describes that the guard electrode is coupled to an operational amplifier, which is further coupled to the working electrode. Fennell at [0032]. However, Fennell is silent with respect to the position of the electrode. The instant claims describe a guard ring that "at least partially surrounds a contact region of the working electrode." As such, Fennell cannot be relied upon to teach the limitations of the instant claims.

Further, Mallas and Schulman fail to cure the deficiencies of Fennell. Mallas and Schulman are silent with respect to the use of a guard ring. Accordingly, Mallas and Schulman are also silent with respect to a guard ring that at least partially surrounds a contact region of the working electrode. Accordingly, Mallas and Schulman cannot be relied upon to teach the limitations of the instant claims, as amended. For at least this reason, Applicant respectfully requests the withdrawal of the 35 U.S.C. § 103 rejections of the claims.
Dependent Claims

Applicant respectfully submits that those dependent claims not discussed separately herein are allowable at least for the reasons discussed with respect to the corresponding independent claims, and respectfully requests that the 35 U.S.C. § 103 rejections thereof be withdrawn.
Conclusion

Applicant submits that the claims, as amended, are in allowable condition and request a corresponding Notice of Allowance. In the event of any outstanding issues, Applicants respectfully request an Examiner Interview to expedite prosecution. Any additional fee that might be due in connection with this application should be applied against Deposit Account No. 50-6159.
